deep.reconstruction:
The page is a five-place table. It continues p.15 and leads into p.17. It has two blocks: arguments 0.560 to 0.600, and 0.600 to 0.640, in steps of 0.001. Each row has five columns: A | B | ΔB | C | ΔC.

What the columns are (identification and checks are mine, not stated on the page):
- A is the argument.
- B = log10(1 + 10^(-A)).
- C = A + B = log10(1 + 10^A).
- ΔB = B(A) − B(A+0.001), in units of 10^-5.
- ΔC = C(A+0.001) − C(A), in units of 10^-5. Since C(A) − A = B(A), it follows that ΔB + ΔC = 100 exactly. Every row on the page satisfies this (e.g. 21+79, 20+80, 19+81, 18+82).

Spot checks against the formula:
- A=0.560: 10^-0.56 = 0.275423, log10(1.275423) = 0.105652, giving 0.10565.
- A=0.587: B = 0.099964, giving 0.09996.
- A=0.600: 10^-0.6 = 0.251189, log10(1.251189) = 0.097323, giving 0.09732.
- A=0.613: giving 0.09474.
- A=0.620: giving 0.09338.
- A=0.634: 10^-0.634 = 0.232274, B = 0.090708, giving 0.09071. This confirms the blotted entry.
- A=0.640: 10^-0.64 = 0.229087, B = 0.089583, giving 0.08958.

The C column is just A + B. Note the cosmetic coincidence that C(0.600) = 0.69732 has the same digits as B = 0.09732 shifted by 0.6.

Purpose: these are Gaussian (addition) logarithms. Given log a and log b with a ≥ b, put A = log a − log b. Then log(a+b) = log a + B(A) = log b + C(A). Read inversely, the table gives log(a−b) by a single entry and one addition. This page is evidently part of the manuscript of Gauss's five-place table, published 1812 in Zach's Monatliche Correspondenz (Werke III). The 1809 bundle date fits that preparation. The difference columns are tabular differences for linear interpolation.
errors: No numerical errors found. All checked B values agree with log10(1+10^-A) to 5 places, all differences are arithmetically consistent with adjacent entries, and ΔB+ΔC=100 throughout.

Several entries in the lower right block (0.09108, 0.09071, 0.09052, 0.09033, 0.09014, 0.08996) are heavily inked or overwritten in the manuscript. This indicates the writer corrected or re-inked them; the final values are correct.

results.what: Five-place table of B(A)=log10(1+10^-A) and C(A)=log10(1+10^A) for A=0.560..0.640 with first differences, for computing the logarithm of a sum or difference from the logarithms of the terms.
results.usually_credited_to: Zecchini Leonelli (idea, 1802/1803); Gauss (first widely used 5-place table, Monatliche Correspondenz 1812)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Gauss's own published 1812 table of addition logarithms, already credited to him (the tables bear his name). It is routine computation with no new mathematics; its only interest is as a working manuscript of the published table.

checkable.asserts: Reproduces the B column on this page (0.10565 at A=0.560 down to 0.08958 at A=0.640).
The blotted entry at A=0.634 is 0.09071.
Identity C(A)=A+B(A) (should simplify to 0), hence ΔB+ΔC=100 units of 1e-5 per 0.001 step.
